newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak parliament ejects dissident deputy.
newsitem.headline: Slovak parliament ejects dissident deputy.

text.p: Slovakia's ruling coalition won a vote in parliament on Wednesday to withdraw the parliamentary mandate of a deputy who defected to protest against what he said was a lack of democracy in the country.

Members of the Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) and junior coalition partners, the Slovak National Party (SNS) and the Workers' Party (ZRS), voted to oust Frantisek Gaulieder after an acrimonious debate in the 150-seat parliament. They won the vote 77-59.
Gaulieder, who had been a founding member of the HZDS, refused to bow to pressure to resign his parliamentary mandate after quitting the party on November 5.

"This is a dangerous precedent which will have a negative impact in the democratic West and will place Slovakia on the level of a banana republic," the leader of the opposition Christian Democratic Movement, Jan Carnogursky, said during the debate.
A Western diplomat said Gaulieder's ousting would be viewed as a "crucial decision".

Slovakia is striving for membership of NATO and the European Union but has received several messages of concern from the West over what is seen as foot-dragging on the path towards democratic reforms.
